person.note:
Graham, W. G. an American, who went to England at the age of seventeen, was sponsored by a chance benefactor through an education and Cambridge and left him a legacy on his death. He eventually returned to America having lost his fortune and he became a journalist for the newspaper The Enquirer. He was killed in a duel. The Times, 21 December 1827 and 25 December 1827.
Godwin records his death and the following entries could also refer to him:
1823-09-27 1824-03-11
The Times says that he did not arrive in England until he was 17 - so, around 1810 - and that he arrived back in America in 1825. For some of these fifteen years he was studying in Cambridge and travelling on the continent. He also lived in London and worked as a parliamentary reporter. There is nothing to suggest that the Glasgow/Edinburgh entries refer to him and I don't think we have enough to link any of the plain Graham entries to him either. We have coded his death and London entries for 1823 and 1824 - these later are supposition but it does seem unlikely that Godwin would have noted his death unless he had met him.
See The Times, 21 December 1827 and 25 December 1827.
